verdict_reason: UPGRADING MY OWN PRIOR YELLOW. There is no source paper -- task_metadata.py marks this 'proxy-only' and cites Miyato 2018 / Virmaux & Scaman 2018 as motivation only -- so the bar is the module docstring's own formula: ratio(l,x_i)=||h_{l+1}(x_i)-h_l(x_i)||/||h_l(x_i)||, L_hat(l)=mean_i ratio, and the reported max = max_l L_hat(l). Against a hand-computed closed form (5 collected layers, 1 token, d=2, h=[(1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(2,2),(99,99)] with the last entry standing in for the post-norm slot) the code returns relative_change_mean 1.3143915862 vs the exact 1.3143915862 (rel 0.00e+00), relative_change_max 2.2360679775 = sqrt(5) exactly, and relative_change_max_layer 2 = argmax -- and it correctly excludes the post-norm entry, which would otherwise have won the argmax at 48.5. Both R13/R14 fixes verified: the four duplicate keys are now _meta_-prefixed and normalization.is_feature('geometry_lipschitz._meta_lipschitz_mean') returns False, so the perfectly collinear columns can no longer reach a BLME feature matrix; and the degenerate branch now emits NaN with nan-aware aggregation for the relative_change_* family (constructed all-zero layer: relative_change_mean = 1.61803 = nanmean([1.0, nan, 2.23607])). The coverage gap and the depth confound are real and severe, but per the campaign's axis rule they are coverage/comparability findings, not implementation infidelity: the code computes the ratio it documents, on the pairs it retains, exactly. (defect_location is CODE because the remaining defects -- the coverage truncation and the half-applied nan-aware aggregation -- live in lipschitz.py rather than in defaults.yaml; neither is verdict-driving, and neither changes the documented ratio on real activations.)
comparable_reason: Re-measured on 7 freshly run models at the shipped config (num_samples=20, WikiText-103 validation): relative_change_mean is 0.5920 (distilgpt2, L=6), 0.8883 (pythia-70m, L=6), 0.3518 (gpt2, L=12), 0.6468 (pythia-160m, L=12), 0.3757 (opt-125m, L=12), 0.2072 (gpt2-medium, L=24), 0.4395 (pythia-410m, L=24). r(mean, n_layers) = -0.697 (p = 0.082), rho = -0.661, r(mean, d_model) = -0.791 (p = 0.034); Spearman is -1 WITHIN BOTH families (gpt2: 0.5920/0.3518/0.2072 at L=6/12/24; pythia: 0.8883/0.6468/0.4395 at L=6/12/24). The mechanism is that the residual-stream norm accumulates with depth while each block's update does not, so ||dh||/||h|| falls roughly as 1/sqrt(l). mean_contraction_rate is worse still: r(n_layers) = -0.852 (p = 0.015), rho = -0.945. A model is therefore rated 'smoother' largely for being deeper. Recovering the missing deepest block with the validated hook does NOT fix this (hook-recovered mean: r(n_layers) = -0.696, r(d_model) = -0.833).
normalized_variant: relative_change_mean_scalenorm (= relative_change_mean x sqrt(n_layers), via the inv_sqrt_n_layers divisor registered in src/blme/normalization.py)
github_repo: avirmaux/lipEstimation (exists, but implements a different quantity)
github_reason: No code was ever released for this statistic; it is a BLME construction and task_metadata is honest about that ('proxy-only'). The repo BLME cites, avirmaux/lipEstimation @336b6cc, implements generic_power_method / _power_method_matrix / lipschitz_spectral_ub -- power-iteration sigma_max and the AutoLip product over layers -- which is a different object from a single-trajectory ||h_{l+1}-h_l||/||h_l||. The repo's own parity fixture in this repo (tests/fixtures/reference_parity/parity/lipschitz.json, and tests/tasks/parity/test_lipschitz_parity.py) says so explicitly and cross-checks the sigma_max kernel that lives in weight_norms.py / spectral.py, NOT in lipschitz.py. NONE is the honest answer rather than PARTIAL.
paper_reason: Miyato et al. 2018 publish spectral-normalization results and Virmaux & Scaman 2018 publish AutoLip/SeqLip bounds; neither publishes a hidden-state relative-change profile for any model, so there is no published value this task could reproduce. The study's own paper does state a formula for it (paper/sections/metrics_geometry.tex line 101) and the code matches that formula, but it also claims an output the code does not emit (see defects).
confounds_reason: See comparable_reason. Over 7 fresh models r(relative_change_mean, n_layers) = -0.697 (p = 0.082) and r(., d_model) = -0.791 (p = 0.034), rho = -0.661 for both; monotone with Spearman -1 within both the gpt2 (distilgpt2/gpt2/gpt2-medium) and pythia (70m/160m/410m) families. mean_contraction_rate: r(n_layers) = -0.852 (p = 0.015), rho = -0.945. Depth and width are collinear in this sample so I cannot separate them. mean_contraction_rate is > 1 on all 7 models (1.0787-1.3471); that is NOT a defect -- a residual stream grows in norm with depth by construction -- but its magnitude above 1 shrinks monotonically with depth, which is exactly the confound.
defects: COVERAGE (CODE). Only L-2 of the L block transitions are measured (verified: n_pairs = 4/6, 4/6, 10/12, 10/12, 10/12, 22/24, 22/24). The embedding->block0 transition is lost because collect_hidden_states drops hidden_states[0], and the deepest block is lost with the post-norm entry. The dropped deepest transition is measurably the LARGEST in the profile in all 7 models: recovered with replace_final_norm=True it is 1.8303 vs a shipped max of 0.9040 on distilgpt2 (2.02x), 4.6698 vs 1.0408 on pythia-70m (4.49x), 1.3579 vs 0.6539 on gpt2 (2.08x), 3.6345 vs 0.7618 on pythia-160m (4.77x), 0.5706 vs 0.5237 on opt-125m (1.09x), 0.5050 vs 0.4860 on gpt2-medium (1.04x), 0.7993 vs 0.7739 on pythia-410m (1.03x). So relative_change_max is currently NOT the max across depth. YES, THE TASK SHOULD ADOPT THE HOOK: I independently validated it, ln_f(hooked layers[-1] output) reproduces HuggingFace's last hidden_states entry to 0.000e+00 on gpt2, distilgpt2 and pythia-70m (while the raw hook output differs from that entry by up to 3.7e+02 / 5.1e+02 / 5.4e+01, i.e. it really is a different, pre-norm representation). Adopting it moves relative_change_mean by +85.1% (pythia-70m), +42.0% (pythia-160m), +41.8% (distilgpt2), +26.0% (gpt2), +6.3% (gpt2-medium), +4.7% (opt-125m), +3.6% (pythia-410m) -- a shift that is itself depth-dependent, so the truncation is currently ADDING to the depth confound.

HALF-APPLIED NaN FIX (CODE, latent). lipschitz.py:164-165 aggregate contraction_rates with np.mean/np.std, not np.nanmean/np.nanstd, while the comment at 130-131 says the aggregates 'must skip them explicitly'. Constructed case with one all-zero layer: relative_change_mean = 1.61803 and relative_change_max = 2.23607 survive correctly, but mean_contraction_rate and contraction_std both become NaN. It never fires on real activations (input norms are O(10)-O(1e3)), so no shipped value is affected -- but the fix is only half done.

DOWNSTREAM KEY BREAK (cross-repo, caused by this round). beyond_benchmarks/scripts/collect_results.py:169-170 reads lip.get('lipschitz_mean') and lip.get('lipschitz_max') -- exactly the two keys just demoted to _meta_lipschitz_*. Both study features will collect as None until that file is updated. The stated justification for the rename ('the study tables carry that key') does not hold either way: geometry_lipschitz is ABSENT from all 66 archived model result JSONs in results/blme_verified_a, and its only archived appearance is a 1-row debug results/feature_matrix.csv carrying lipschitz_mean 7.293 / lipschitz_max 32.720 for pythia-70m -- pre-drop values contaminated by the ln_f pair, which I re-measure at 28.407, i.e. 27.3x the largest real transition in that model.

PAPER-VS-CODE MISMATCH. paper/sections/metrics_geometry.tex line 101 and metrics_catalogue.tex line 31 both say the task reports 'the fraction of contractive transitions (L_l < 1)'. The code computes no such fraction: it emits mean_contraction_rate = mean over layers of mean over tokens of ||h_{l+1}||/||h_l||, a norm-GROWTH ratio which is > 1 on all 7 models (1.0787-1.3471), plus contraction_std. Either add the fraction or correct the paper.

relative_change_max_layer is the index of the LOWER member of the winning pair in collected-key space (block i -> block i+1), which is documented nowhere; and it sits at the truncation boundary (the last measured pair) in 3 of 7 models -- gpt2 9/10, opt-125m 9/10, gpt2-medium 21/22 -- consistent with the profile still rising where the code stops looking.

The four _meta_lipschitz_* aliases still carry BIT-IDENTICAL duplicates of the relative_change_* values (verified equal on the analytic case). Inside BLME that is now harmless because normalization.is_feature() excludes any key containing '_meta_'; outside BLME nothing enforces it.
The parity fixture tests/fixtures/reference_parity/parity/lipschitz.json cites 'lipschitz.py lines 37-40, 112-115' for the disclaimer; those line numbers moved with this round's edit.
fix: (1) Pass replace_final_norm=True in lipschitz.py's collect_hidden_states call and drop the collected_layer_count truncation, restoring blocks 0..L-1 (L-1 of L transitions); optionally also keep hidden_states[0] to recover embedding->block0 and reach full L. This is the single most valuable change: it recovers what is measurably the largest transition, and it is validated to 0.000e+00 against ln_f. (2) Replace np.mean/np.std with np.nanmean/np.nanstd for contraction_rates and add a _meta_n_skipped_layers count. (3) NORMALIZED TWIN -- none exists today (NORMALIZERS in src/blme/normalization.py has no lipschitz or relative_change entry, so normalized_variant is empty and normalized_ok is ABSENT). The twin that actually fixes the depth confound is relative_change_mean MULTIPLIED by sqrt(n_layers), i.e. the 1/sqrt(l) growth of the residual norm undone: measured values 1.4501 / 2.1759 / 1.2186 / 2.2405 / 1.3016 / 1.0149 / 2.1531 give r(n_layers) = -0.151 (p = 0.747) and r(d_model) = -0.305 (p = 0.506), down from -0.697 and -0.791 raw, and the pythia family becomes flat (2.176 / 2.241 / 2.153 at L = 6/12/24) while the family separation (gpt2/opt ~1.0-1.45 vs pythia ~2.15-2.24) survives. Note normalization.add_normalized() can only DIVIDE by a named divisor and arch_info() offers no 1/sqrt(n_layers), so registering this twin needs a new divisor key (e.g. inv_sqrt_n_layers = 1/sqrt(L)). REFUTING MY OWN PRIOR SUGGESTION: reporting the ratio at fixed normalized depths does NOT fix the confound -- the profile value at 25/50/75% depth has r(n_layers) = -0.510 / -0.656 / -0.724, essentially as confounded as the mean. (4) Update beyond_benchmarks/scripts/collect_results.py:169-170 to read relative_change_mean / relative_change_max. (5) Fix the paper's 'fraction of contractive transitions' claim. (6) RE-RUN is moot for the 66-model sweep (the task produced no output there at all) but the 1-row debug feature_matrix.csv is stale and must not be reused. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): the twin proposed in item (3) is now registered as relative_change_mean_scalenorm and it is YELLOW -- it works, but not for the reason given. It works: over 20 freshly run models at the shipped config raw relative_change_mean has rho(n_layers) = -0.583 (p = 0.007) and the twin -0.130 (p = 0.6), with rho(d_model) -0.091 -> +0.012 and rho(vocab) +0.226 -> +0.283, so it removes the depth term without introducing another. But the exponent is fitted, not derived. The registered rationale requires ||h_l|| ~ sqrt(l) with a depth-independent block update; measured across 9 models the residual norm grows as l^+0.82 (range +0.56 on gpt2-medium to +1.21 on SmolLM2-135M), and the per-block ratio profile exponent runs from +0.44 (pythia-70m) to -0.30 (gpt2-large), i.e. in shallow models the ratio RISES with depth rather than falling as 1/sqrt(l). Across models the metric goes as L^-0.647, so sqrt(L) supplies about half the correction the data asks for and leaves a residual L^-0.15 (a factor 0.68 from L = 6 to L = 64). Keep the twin, but document it as an empirical half-power rather than as the 1/sqrt(l) law, and expect a residual depth term on a zoo with a wider depth range than this panel.
